hook: Hyderabad reuses just *3.5%* of the sewage it treats
hook_b: Hyderabad reuses just *3.5%* of the sewage it treats
tldr: A 2025 study comparing Japan and India found Hyderabad reuses 27 MLD of the 772 MLD of sewage it treats, 3.5%, against a 20% central benchmark. HMWSSB plans tenders next month to supply treated water to data centres and industry.

beats.what: A study and HMWSSB figures show most of Hyderabad's treated wastewater is not reused.
beats.why: The city faces water shortages and growing tanker use amid El Niño and deficit rain.
beats.care: HMWSSB launched green tankers for construction and gardening on Nov 1 and plans grey-water filling stations.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 19): the board aims for the 20% benchmark in 18 months and will invite tenders next month.

cards.q: Where should Hyderabad's treated wastewater go first?

qs: Who should pay for pipelines carrying treated water to industries?
Could treated water refill Hyderabad lakes as in Bengaluru?

facts.t: HMWSSB says its treatment capacity doubled from over 700 MLD in 2025 to about *1,400 MLD*, yet ~30 MLD is recycled.

viz.verdict: Most treated water flows into drains while the city uses tankers

watch: HMWSSB tenders next month for supplying treated water to data centres and industries.

sources.title: Hyderabad reuses just 3.5% of treated wastewater, shows study

fact: Hyderabad reuses only *27 of 772 MLD* of treated sewage, a study finds
twist: The water board puts it even lower, at about 2%, despite doubling treatment capacity this year.
